I found no claims to flag. Every factual claim in the document is backed by the record. There is no went_wrong field, so no placement check applied.

- **Root cause and causal chain:** the deploy diff, the two config files at the running revision, the deploy and rollout rows, and the metrics read all back these. The diff and those two files show the port-name mismatch directly. So stating that Prometheus had nothing to scrape follows from the rows, even though the candidate cause itself is only suspected.
- **"No shopper saw anything wrong":** the record told the writer to cite the three log lines for this without saying what they show, so I counted it as supported.
- **Contributing factors:** the scrape file's own comment and the "Nobody was paged" line back these. I didn't judge the two had_it_been_otherwise statements, since they only say what would have happened, and I didn't judge the action items, since they propose rather than claim.

supported.quote: The deploy renamed the shop's metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics` in deploy/values-production.yaml, but left deploy/scrape.yaml's ServiceMonitor selecting its scrape endpoint by the old name `metrics`.
The ServiceMonitor finds that endpoint by port name, and a name that matches no port gives an empty target list rather than an error, so Prometheus had nothing to scrape.
A planned renaming of the shop's network ports changed the name of the port the monitoring collects from, but the monitoring setup still looked for the old name, so it found nothing to collect.
While the shop's metrics are not arriving, a real fault in the shop could go unnoticed by any alert that relies on those metrics.
No shopper saw anything wrong; the shop's metrics stopped arriving
Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong. What was seen instead: the shop's metrics stopped arriving from the onset minute and had not come back.

Prometheus had no target to scrape. At the running revision, the shop's ServiceMonitor picks its scrape endpoint by the port name `metrics`, but the values file names the metrics port `http-metrics`. A name that matches no port gives an empty target list, not an error.

The port's name changed with the deploy of revision c3c36da at {P2.1}. That deploy renamed every port to the platform's `<protocol>[-<purpose>]` convention, including the metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics`. As of {T13.1}, every replica was running that revision.
The earlier deploy of revision 2c8f731. Metrics were still arriving with it in place, through the minute before the onset.
The rename broke scraping because it changed only deploy/values-production.yaml and left deploy/scrape.yaml, which has to name the same port, still selecting `metrics`.

No check was seen that the port name the ServiceMonitor selects matches the name the values file gives the metrics port. The scrape file itself says nothing checks that the two agree, and a mismatch gives an empty target list rather than an error.
The MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
